label: ex:BMOA-local-dichotomy
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:BMOA-local-dichotomy}
Let $r>0$, $\phi(z)=2+z$ and $\varphi(z)=z$. Then
\[
 D_{2+z,\operatorname{id}}^1:BMOA=F(2,0,1)
               \longrightarrow F(r,2r-2,1)
\]
is bounded if and only if $r\ge2$. Whenever it is bounded, it is not
compact. More precisely, for $r\ge2$,
$\mathcal C_{2,1;r}(\{v_{a,j,l}:j\ge J\})\approx1$ uniformly in
$a\in\mathbb D$ and $J\ge0$.
head: environment

label: eq:local-example-array
title: Proof
body_md:
All target triples are admissible. Here $b_1=1$, $\phi'=1$ and
$1\le|2+z|\le3$, while
\[
 d\lambda_a(z)=(1-|z|^2)^{2r-1}
                     \frac{1-|a|^2}{|1-\overline az|^2}\,dA(z).
\]
On $Q_{j,l}$, the two terms of $v_a$ are comparable to
$\delta_j^{r+1}$ and $\delta_j$, respectively, times the same kernel.
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-example-array}
 v_{a,j,l}\approx\delta_j
                \frac{1-|a|^2}{|1-\overline a a_{j,l}|^2},
\end{equation}
with constants independent of $a,j,l$.

Suppose $r\ge2$. If $\zeta\in I_{j,l}$, then
$|1-\overline a\zeta|\le C|1-\overline a a_{j,l}|$:
use $|\zeta-a_{j,l}|\le C\delta_j$ and
$|1-\overline a a_{j,l}|\ge3\delta_j/4$.
Along the nested arcs containing $\zeta$, the marked points tend to
$\zeta$. Since $|I_{j,l}|=\delta_j/8$, formula
\eqref{eq:critical-shadow-maximal} therefore gives, for every $J$,
\[
 \mathcal C_{2,1;r}(\{v_{a,j,l}:j\ge J\})
 \approx\int_{\partial\mathbb D}
              \frac{1-|a|^2}{|1-\overline a\zeta|^2}\,dm(\zeta)=1.
\]
Theorems~\ref{thm:F-boundedness} and \ref{thm:F-essential-norm}
prove boundedness and noncompactness.

If $r<2$, take $a=0$, so that $v_{0,j,l}\approx\delta_j$.
In \eqref{eq:tree-mass-constraints}, put $x_I=|I|/K$ on $K$
consecutive full levels and zero elsewhere. Every subtree constraint
holds, and the objective is comparable to $K^{1-r/2}$.
Letting $K\to\infty$ gives $\mathcal C_{2,1;r}(v_0)=\infty$, which
proves unboundedness.

For a direct boundedness check, the local Cauchy estimate gives
$\|h\|_{F(2,2,1)}\le C\|f\|_{BMOA}$ for $h=(2+z)f'$;
apply it to $f'$ on enlarged squares and use bounded overlap.
The same estimate gives $(1-|z|^2)^2|h'(z)|\le C\|f\|_{BMOA}$.
For $r\ge2$, multiplying the square integrand for $F(2,2,1)$ by
$((1-|z|^2)^2|h'|)^{r-2}$ proves the claimed $F(r,2r-2,1)$ bound.
The noncompactness also has a direct test. The polynomials $f_k=z^k$
have bounded $BMOA$ norms and tend locally to zero. For
$h_k=(2+z)f_k'$, one has
$h_k'=kz^{k-2}(2(k-1)+kz)$. On
$1-1/k<|z|<1-1/(2k)$, $k\ge4$, its modulus is at least $ck^2$.
The defining target integral at $a=0$ is therefore at least
$c_r k^{2r}k^{-(2r-1)}k^{-1}=c_r>0$.
Thus these images cannot have a norm-convergent subsequence.
head: environment

label: thm:F-comparison
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:F-comparison}
Let $0<p_i<\infty$, $q_i>-2$, $s_i\ge0$ and $q_i+s_i>-1$ for
$i=1,2$, and let $n\ge1$. Suppose
$D_{\phi,\varphi}^n:F(p_1,q_1,s_1)\to F(p_2,q_2,s_2)$ is bounded.
For $0\le h\le k$, the same formula defines a bounded operator
\[
 D_{\phi,\varphi}^n:
 F(p_1,q_1+p_1h,s_1)\longrightarrow F(p_2,q_2+p_2k,s_2).
\]
Its operator norm and essential norm are at most
$C((1+|\varphi(0)|)/(1-|\varphi(0)|))^h$ times the respective
original norms. In particular, compactness is preserved. If $k>h$,
the shifted operator is compact even when the original operator is
only bounded; if also $s_2>0$, it is compact with codomain
$F_0(p_2,q_2+p_2k,s_2)$.

For $s_1>0$ the norm comparisons hold with both sources little.
For $s_1,s_2>0$ they also hold with both sources and both targets
little, provided the original little-space operator is bounded.
Constants depend only on the fixed parameters, $n,h,k$ and the partition.
head: environment

label: eq:comparison-Schwarz-Pick
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $b=\varphi(0)$ and $K=(1+|b|)/(1-|b|)$. Schwarz--Pick gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:comparison-Schwarz-Pick}
 1-|z|^2\le1-|\sigma_b(\varphi(z))|^2
 =\frac{(1-|b|^2)(1-|\varphi(z)|^2)}
        {|1-\overline b\varphi(z)|^2}
 \le K(1-|\varphi(z)|^2).
\end{equation}
In particular, $1-|z|^2\le2K\delta_j$ when
$\varphi(z)\in Q_{j,l}$; see also \cite{CowenMacCluer1995}.
For the shifted spaces, the target weight is
$(1-|z|^2)^{p_2k}d\lambda_a(z)$ and the source exponent is $b_n+h$.
Write $v_a^{(h,k)}$ for the resulting array. Since $k\ge h$,
\[
 v_{a,j,l}^{(h,k)}\le(2K)^{p_2h}v_{a,j,l},\qquad
 v_{a,j,l}^{(h,k)}\le(2K)^{p_2k}
                      \delta_j^{p_2(k-h)}v_{a,j,l}.
\]
The first inequality uses $(1-|z|^2)^{p_2(k-h)}\le1$; the second
uses \eqref{eq:comparison-Schwarz-Pick} on the full additional weight.
The source sequence space $\mathcal E_{p_1,s_1}$ is unchanged.
Thus monotonicity and homogeneity of $\mathfrak D$, followed by
Proposition~\ref{prop:explicit-sequence}, control both the full
sequence quantity and each tail. The scalar term satisfies
\[
 \frac{|\phi(0)|}{(1-|b|^2)^{b_n+h}}
       \le K^h\frac{|\phi(0)|}{(1-|b|^2)^{b_n}}.
\]
Theorems~\ref{thm:F-boundedness} and \ref{thm:F-essential-norm}
now give the norm comparisons. If $k>h$, the second array inequality
bounds the shifted tail, after taking its $p_2$th root, by
$C K^k2^{-J(k-h)}\sup_a\mathfrak D_{p_1,s_1;p_2}(v_a)$.
It tends to zero, proving compactness.

If $s>0$ and $u>0$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-weight-little}
 F(p,q,s)\subset F_0(p,q+pu,s).
\end{equation}
Indeed, on $|z|>R$ the new defining integral is at most
$(1-R^2)^{pu}\|f\|_{F(p,q,s)}^p$, uniformly in its local parameter.
On $|z|\le R$ its kernel tends uniformly to zero as $|a|\uparrow1$.
Let first $|a|\uparrow1$ and then $R\uparrow1$.
For $k>h$, the polynomial tests give
$\phi,\phi\varphi\in F(p_2,q_2,s_2)$, and $k>0$ puts both functions
in the shifted little target by \eqref{eq:strict-weight-little}.
Together with the vanishing shifted tail,
Theorem~\ref{thm:F-little-operators}(b) gives compactness into that
target, also when $s_1=0$.

For little sources, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:F-little-operators}(a).
For little sources and targets, its part (b) applies because increasing
the weight exponent preserves the two little-space memberships.
The same sequence comparisons then prove the claimed norm bounds.
head: environment

label: thm:supremum-targets
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:supremum-targets}
Let $X$, the integer $n$, and the exponent $b$ be chosen from
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 X&n&b\\ \hline
 H(p,q,\alpha)&n\ge0&\alpha+1/p+n\\
 S(p,q,\alpha)&n\ge1&\alpha+1/p+n-1\\
 F(p,q,s)\text{ or }F_0(p,q,s)&n\ge1&(q+2)/p+n-1.
\end{array}
\]
Let $\phi\in H(\mathbb D)$ and let $\varphi$ be an analytic self-map.
Then:

\textup{(a)} $D_{\phi,\varphi}^n:X\to H^\infty$ is bounded if and only if
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb D}
       \frac{|\phi(z)|}{(1-|\varphi(z)|^2)^b}<\infty,
\]
and its norm is comparable to this supremum.

\textup{(b)} $D_{\phi,\varphi}^n:X\to S^\infty$ is bounded if and only if
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb D}\left(
       \frac{|\phi'(z)|}{(1-|\varphi(z)|^2)^b}
       +\frac{|\phi(z)\varphi'(z)|}{(1-|\varphi(z)|^2)^{b+1}}
                       \right)<\infty.
\]
Its norm is comparable to this supremum plus
$|\phi(0)|(1-|\varphi(0)|^2)^{-b}$.

In either part, under boundedness the essential norm is comparable to
the limiting supremum of the displayed pointwise expression over
$\{z:|\varphi(z)|>R\}$ as $R\uparrow1$. Thus compactness is equivalent
to that limit being zero. The supremum of an empty set is taken as zero.
All comparison constants depend only on the source parameters and $n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The sampling and synthesis estimates give
\[
 \sup_{\|f\|_X\le1}|f^{(n)}(w)|\approx(1-|w|^2)^{-b},
 \qquad
 \sup_{\|f\|_X\le1}|f^{(n+1)}(w)|\approx(1-|w|^2)^{-b-1}.
\]
For a mixed-norm source use Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-estimates}; for
its derivative space integrate the kernels once; for the $F$ sources
use Lemma~\ref{lem:F-sampling-synthesis}. The one-kernel test functions
are analytic past the closed disk, so the lower bounds apply to the
little source as well. Taking suprema proves (a).

The product rule and these estimates prove the upper bound in (b).
For its reverse bound, fix $z$ and choose the rectangle containing
$\varphi(z)$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:two-kernels} to
$x=\phi'(z)$ and $y=\phi(z)\varphi'(z)$, using the two kernels for a
mixed-norm source and their primitives for a derivative source.
For the former use that lemma with derivative orders $n,n+1$;
for the latter use orders $n-1,n$. Their source norms are uniformly
bounded by the same synthesis estimates. This bounds the two-term
pointwise expression by $C\|D_{\phi,\varphi}^n\|$. Evaluation at zero
supplies the remaining scalar term.

For the essential-norm upper bound use the compact approximants
$D_{\phi,\varphi}^nC_\rho$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:space-basics}.
On $|\varphi(z)|\le R$, the needed derivatives of $f-C_\rho f$
converge uniformly to zero on the source unit ball. The coefficient
functions are bounded: polynomial tests give $\phi\in H^\infty$
in (a), and $\phi,\phi\varphi\in S^\infty$ in (b), which also gives
$\phi\varphi'\in H^\infty$. On the complement use the displayed
pointwise expression and the uniformly bounded source quasi-norm of
$f-C_\rho f$. The value at zero in (b) also tends to zero. Let first
$\rho\uparrow1$ and then $R\uparrow1$.

For a positive boundary limit, choose $z_j$ with
$|\varphi(z_j)|\to1$ realizing a fixed fraction of that limit. The
one-kernel test in (a), or one of the two kernels in (b), gives functions
of uniformly bounded source norm whose image norms are bounded below
by a fixed fraction of the limit. Choose the kernel order sufficiently
large as in the synthesis lemmas. Their local tail estimates show that
the functions and their fixed derivatives tend locally to zero, and
so do their images. Lemma~\ref{lem:essential-test}, with target
$H^\infty$ or $S^\infty$, proves the lower bound and the compactness
criterion.
head: environment

label: prop:subcritical-zero-order
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:subcritical-zero-order}
Let $X$ be $S(p,q,\alpha)$ with $\alpha+1/p<1$, or $F(p,q,s)$
with $(q+2)/p<1$, in the parameter ranges above; the little $F$
source is also allowed. For every analytic self-map $\varphi$ and
$0<r\le\infty$,
\[
 D_{\phi,\varphi}^0:X\to H^r\text{ bounded}
 \iff D_{\phi,\varphi}^0:X\to H^r\text{ compact}
 \iff \phi\in H^r.
\]
Its norm is comparable to $\|\phi\|_{H^r}$, uniformly in $\varphi$.

For the source $S(p,q,\alpha)$ in this subcritical range,
$D_{\phi,\varphi}^0:S(p,q,\alpha)\to S^r$ is bounded if and only if
$\phi\in S^r$ and
$D_{\phi\varphi',\varphi}^0:H(p,q,\alpha)\to H^r$ is bounded.
Its norm is comparable to $\|\phi\|_{S^r}$ plus the norm of this last
operator, and their essential norms are equal. Thus
Theorem~\ref{thm:mixed-hardy} (or Theorem~\ref{thm:supremum-targets}
when $r=\infty$) gives an explicit criterion at order zero. If $q>r$, boundedness
also implies compactness in this derivative-target assertion.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In each source, $|f'(z)|\le C\|f\|_X(1-|z|)^{-a}$ for some
$0<a<1$. Radial integration gives $\|f\|_\infty\le C\|f\|_X$ and
\[
 \|f-C_\rho f\|_\infty
       \le \frac{C}{1-a}(1-\rho)^{1-a}\|f\|_X.
\]
Indeed, integrate $zf'(tz)$ for $\rho\le t\le1$ and use
$1-t|z|\ge1-t$. A fixed $C_\rho:X\to H^\infty$ is compact by
local normality. The displayed estimate therefore makes the inclusion
$X\to H^\infty$ compact. The map $h\mapsto\phi(h\circ\varphi)$ from
$H^\infty$ to $H^r$ has norm $\|\phi\|_{H^r}$ when $\phi\in H^r$.
Composition proves sufficiency and compactness, and the test $1$
proves necessity and the lower norm bound.

For the derivative target, testing $1$ gives $\phi\in S^r$.
The just proved compact inclusion makes
$f\mapsto\phi'(f\circ\varphi):S(p,q,\alpha)\to H^r$ compact.
The identity
\[
 (D_{\phi,\varphi}^0f)'=
       \phi'(f\circ\varphi)+D_{\phi\varphi',\varphi}^0(f')
\]
and the primitive right inverse therefore prove the boundedness
criterion and both norm inequalities. The scalar value at zero is
finite rank. After integrating the displayed identity, the difference
between $D_{\phi,\varphi}^0$ and
$J D_{\phi\varphi',\varphi}^0\partial$ is compact.
Differentiation and $J$ are contractions in both directions between
the relevant derivative spaces and their derivative components.
Composing compact approximants with these maps proves equality of
essential norms, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-reduction}.
head: environment

label: thm:relatively-compact-symbol
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:relatively-compact-symbol}
Let $X,Y$ be any of the source and target spaces just specified.
Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, let $\phi\in H(\mathbb D)$, and let
$\varphi$ be an analytic self-map of $\mathbb D$ with
$\|\varphi\|_\infty<1$. The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
 \renewcommand{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}
 \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
 \item $D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}:X\to Y$ is bounded.
 \item $D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}:X\to Y$ is compact.
 \item If $Y=H^r$, then $\phi\in H^r$. For any of the derivative
       targets $S^r$, $F(p_2,q_2,s_2)$ and $F_0(p_2,q_2,s_2)$,
       one has $\phi,\phi\varphi\in Y$.
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold,
\[
 \|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}\|_{X\to Y}
 \approx
 \begin{cases}
  \|\phi\|_{H^r},&Y=H^r,\\
  \|\phi\|_Y+\|\phi\varphi\|_Y,&
       Y=S^r,\ F(p_2,q_2,s_2)\text{ or }F_0(p_2,q_2,s_2).
 \end{cases}
\]
For each fixed $0<\rho<1$, the comparison constants can be chosen
uniformly for $\|\varphi\|_\infty\le\rho$; they depend only on
$\rho$, $n$ and the parameters of $X,Y$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Each source contains the polynomials. Testing (1) on $z^n/n!$ gives
$\phi\in Y$, and testing it on $z^{n+1}/(n+1)!$ gives
$\phi\varphi\in Y$. For $Y=H^r$, the second membership already
follows from the first because $|\varphi|\le1$. These tests prove
(1)$\Rightarrow$(3), as well as the lower operator-norm estimates.
They include $n=0$, with the usual convention $0!=1$.

Suppose (3) holds, and fix $0<\rho<1$ with
$\|\varphi\|_\infty\le\rho$. The local estimate \eqref{eq:source-local-interior} holds on each
listed source, and on its little subspace by restriction.

If $Y=H^r$, take $m=n$ in \eqref{eq:source-local-interior}. Then
$|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f(z)|\le C\|f\|_X|\phi(z)|$ for every
$z\in\mathbb D$, so
$\|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f\|_{H^r}\le C\|\phi\|_{H^r}\|f\|_X$.
This proves boundedness and the upper norm estimate for this target.

Consider a derivative target. The product rule gives
\[
 (D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f)'
   =\phi'(f^{(n)}\circ\varphi)
                +\phi\varphi'(f^{(n+1)}\circ\varphi).
\]
Since $\phi\varphi'=(\phi\varphi)'-\phi'\varphi$, the local estimates
with $m=n,n+1$ imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |(D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f)'(z)|
  &\le C\|f\|_X\bigl(|\phi'(z)|+|(\phi\varphi)'(z)|\bigr),\\
 |D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f(0)|
  &\le C\|f\|_X|\phi(0)|.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For $Y=S^r$, take Hardy means of the derivative, or its supremum
when $r=\infty$. For a large $F$
target, integrate its $p_2$th power against $\lambda_a$ and take the
supremum over $a$. In either case, the defining quasi-norm and the
inequality for a power of a sum give
\[
 \|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f\|_Y
       \le C\bigl(\|\phi\|_Y+\|\phi\varphi\|_Y\bigr)\|f\|_X.
\]
For $Y=F_0(p_2,q_2,s_2)$ the same bound holds in the large space.
Moreover, the two defining derivative integrals for $\phi$ and
$\phi\varphi$ tend to zero as $|a|\uparrow1$. The displayed
pointwise estimate therefore puts $D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f$ in the
little target as well. This proves (3)$\Rightarrow$(1) and all the
upper norm estimates.
It remains to prove compactness under (3). Choose
$\|\varphi\|_\infty<\eta<1$. The function $\varphi/\eta$ is an
analytic self-map with relatively compact range, and
$\phi(\varphi/\eta)=\eta^{-1}\phi\varphi$. Thus the boundedness
implication already proved applies to
$D_{\phi,\varphi/\eta}^{n}:X\to Y$. Direct differentiation gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:interior-factorization}
 D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}
       =\eta^{-n}D_{\phi,\varphi/\eta}^{n}C_\eta,
                \qquad C_\eta f(z)=f(\eta z).
\end{equation}
The dilation is compact by Lemmas~\ref{lem:space-basics} and
\ref{lem:F-little-approximation}.
The factorization proves (3)$\Rightarrow$(2), and
(2)$\Rightarrow$(1) is immediate. Uniformity of the norm constants
follows from \eqref{eq:source-local-interior} and the two polynomial
tests.

label: cor:Dirichlet-interior
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:relatively-compact-symbol} with
both spaces equal to $F(2,\beta,0)$. Since $\phi'\varphi\in A_\beta^2$, the identity
$(\phi\varphi)'=\phi'\varphi+\phi\varphi'$ gives the last equivalence.
head: environment

label: lem:F-multiplier-bound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:F-multiplier-bound}
Let $0<p<\infty$, $q>-2$, $s\ge0$ and $q+s>-1$. Let $X$ be
$F(p,q,s)$, or $F_0(p,q,s)$ when $s>0$. If $g\in\mathcal M(X)$,
then $M_g:X\to X$ is bounded and
$\|g\|_\infty\le\|M_g\|_{X\to X}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemmas~\ref{lem:F-dilations} and \ref{lem:F-little-approximation},
$X$ is a quasi-Banach space, and convergence in $X$ implies local
uniform convergence. The graph of $M_g$ is closed: if $f_j\to f$ and
$gf_j\to h$ in $X$, their local limits give $h=gf$. The closed graph
theorem for quasi-Banach spaces therefore makes $M_g$ bounded; see
\cite{KaltonPeckRoberts1984}. This version of the theorem does not
require local convexity.

For $w\in\mathbb D$, the evaluation $e_w(f)=f(w)$ is a continuous
linear functional on $X$. It is nonzero because $1\in X$. The identity
$e_wM_g=g(w)e_w$ gives
\[
 |g(w)|\|e_w\|_{X^*}
     =\|e_wM_g\|_{X^*}
     \le\|e_w\|_{X^*}\|M_g\|_{X\to X}.
\]
Cancel $\|e_w\|_{X^*}>0$ and take the supremum over $w$.
head: environment

label: thm:F-all-weights
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:F-all-weights}
Let $0<p<\infty$, $q>-2$, $s\ge0$ and $q+s>-1$. Let $X$ be
$F(p,q,s)$, or $F_0(p,q,s)$ when $s>0$. Fix an integer $n\ge1$
and an analytic self-map $\varphi$ of $\mathbb D$. The following
conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
 \renewcommand{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}
 \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
 \item For every $\phi\in X$, the operator
       $D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}:X\to X$ is bounded.
 \item For every $\phi\in X$, the operator
       $D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}:X\to X$ is compact.
 \item $\|\varphi\|_\infty<1$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal M(X)$.
\end{enumerate}
Under these conditions, for every fixed $0<\rho<1$ with
$\|\varphi\|_\infty\le\rho$ and every $\phi\in X$,
\[
 c\|\phi\|_X
   \le\|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}\|_{X\to X}
   \le C_\rho\bigl(1+\|\varphi\|_{\mathcal M(X)}\bigr)\|\phi\|_X.
\]
Here $c>0$ depends only on $X,n$, and $C_\rho$ depends only on
$X,n,\rho$, not on the two symbols. In \textup{(1)} no uniform bound
on the operator norms as $\phi$ varies is assumed.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose (1) holds. For each fixed $f\in X$, the function
$g=f^{(n)}\circ\varphi$ satisfies
$g\phi=D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f\in X$ for every $\phi\in X$.
Thus $g\in\mathcal M(X)$ and, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:F-multiplier-bound}, $g\in H^\infty$.

Consider the linear map $f\mapsto f^{(n)}\circ\varphi$ from $X$ to
$H^\infty$. Its graph is closed. Indeed, if $f_j\to f$ in $X$ and
$f_j^{(n)}\circ\varphi\to h$ in $H^\infty$, local uniform convergence
of the derivatives gives $h(z)=f^{(n)}(\varphi(z))$ for every
$z\in\mathbb D$. The closed graph theorem, now with codomain
$H^\infty$, supplies a constant $C$ depending on $X,n,\varphi$ such
that
\[
 \|f^{(n)}\circ\varphi\|_\infty\le C\|f\|_X,
                         \qquad f\in X.
\]
For the large space, the derivative-evaluation estimate is
\eqref{eq:F-derivative-evaluation}. It holds with the same comparison
constants on the little space: the upper bound follows by restriction,
and the one-kernel primitives used for the lower bound are analytic
past $\overline{\mathbb D}$, so belong to the little space by
Lemma~\ref{lem:F-little-approximation}. Consequently,
\[
 (1-|\varphi(z)|^2)^{-(q+2)/p-n+1}
   \le C'\sup_{\|f\|_X\le1}|f^{(n)}(\varphi(z))|
   \le C'',\qquad z\in\mathbb D.
\]
The exponent $(q+2)/p+n-1$ is positive. Hence
$\|\varphi\|_\infty<1$.

The polynomial $f(z)=z^{n+1}/(n+1)!$ belongs to $X$. Applying (1) to
this $f$ gives $\phi\varphi\in X$ for every $\phi\in X$.
Thus $\varphi\in\mathcal M(X)$, proving (3).

Conversely, suppose (3) holds and fix $\phi\in X$.
Then $\phi,\phi\varphi\in X$. Theorem~\ref{thm:relatively-compact-symbol},
with this source and target, proves that $D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}$ is
compact. This proves (3)$\Rightarrow$(2); the implication
(2)$\Rightarrow$(1) is immediate.

Finally, the upper estimate in
Theorem~\ref{thm:relatively-compact-symbol} gives
\[
 \|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}\|_{X\to X}
   \le C_\rho\bigl(\|\phi\|_X+\|\phi\varphi\|_X\bigr)
   \le C_\rho\bigl(1+\|\varphi\|_{\mathcal M(X)}\bigr)\|\phi\|_X.
\]
Testing on $z^n/n!$, whose image is $\phi$, proves the lower estimate.
head: environment

label: thm:interior-approximation
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:interior-approximation}
Let $X,Y$ be any of the source and target spaces specified before
Theorem~\ref{thm:relatively-compact-symbol}. Let $n\ge0$ be an integer,
let $\phi\in H(\mathbb D)$, and let $\varphi$ be an analytic self-map
of $\mathbb D$ with $\|\varphi\|_\infty<1$. Suppose that
$D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}:X\to Y$ is bounded.
\begin{enumerate}
 \renewcommand{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}
 \setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
 \item For $0<\rho<\eta<1$ with $\|\varphi\|_\infty\le\rho$,
 \[
  a_N(D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n})
       \le C\eta^N\|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}\|_{X\to Y},
                          \qquad N\ge1.
 \]
 The constant depends only on $X,Y,n,\rho,\eta$, not on the symbols
 or $N$. In particular,
 \[
  \limsup_{N\to\infty}a_N(D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n})^{1/N}
                         \le\|\varphi\|_\infty.
 \]
 \item Put $\ell_k(f)=f^{(n+k)}(0)/k!$ and
 $y_k=\phi\varphi^k$, with $\varphi^0=1$. Then $\ell_k\in X^*$,
 $y_k\in Y$, and
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:interior-rank-one}
  D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}
       =\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\ell_k\otimes y_k,
       \qquad (\ell_k\otimes y_k)f=\ell_k(f)y_k,
 \end{equation}
 with convergence in the operator quasi-norm. Moreover,
 \[
  \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
        (\|\ell_k\|_{X^*}\|y_k\|_Y)^t<\infty
                         \qquad\text{for every }t>0.
 \]
 Consequently, when $X,Y$ are Banach spaces, the operator is
 $t$-nuclear for every $0<t\le1$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, every bounded operator of this form from
$\mathcal D_{\beta_1}$ to $\mathcal D_{\beta_2}$, with
$\beta_1,\beta_2>-1$ and $\|\varphi\|_\infty<1$, belongs to all
Schatten classes $\mathcal S_t$, $t>0$.
head: environment

label: eq:interior-coefficient-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\rho<\eta<1$ as in (1), and choose a radius $R$ with
$\rho/\eta<R<1$. In particular, $\rho<R$ and $\rho/R<\eta$.
Cauchy's coefficient formula for $f^{(n)}$, together with
\eqref{eq:source-local-interior}, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:interior-coefficient-bound}
 |\ell_k(f)|\le R^{-k}\max_{|w|=R}|f^{(n)}(w)|
       \le C_{R,n,X}R^{-k}\|f\|_X,\qquad k\ge0.
\end{equation}
Thus $\ell_k\in X^*$ for every listed source.

For brevity put
\[
 B=\begin{cases}
       \|\phi\|_{H^r},&Y=H^r,\\
       \|\phi\|_Y+\|\phi\varphi\|_Y,&\text{otherwise}.
    \end{cases}
\]
The polynomial tests in Theorem~\ref{thm:relatively-compact-symbol}
give $B\le C_{X,n}\|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}\|_{X\to Y}$.
The same theorem's derivative calculation shows, for every
$u\in H(\mathbb D)$, that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:interior-target-bound}
 \|\phi(u\circ\varphi)\|_Y
     \le C_Y B\left(\max_{|w|\le\rho}|u(w)|
                          +\max_{|w|\le\rho}|u'(w)|\right).
\end{equation}
For $H^r$ only the first maximum is needed. For a derivative target
use the product rule and $\phi\varphi'=(\phi\varphi)'-\phi'\varphi$;
the same estimate preserves the defining vanishing integrals of a
little target.
Taking $u(w)=w^k$ gives $y_k\in Y$ and
\[
 \|y_k\|_Y\le C_{Y,\rho}B(k+1)\rho^k,\qquad k\ge0.
\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:interior-coefficient-bound}, for every $t>0$,
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(\|\ell_k\|_{X^*}\|y_k\|_Y)^t
       \le C B^t\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(k+1)^t(\rho/R)^{kt}<\infty.
\]

For $N\ge0$, put
\[
 K_Nf=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\ell_k(f)y_k,\qquad
 u_{N,f}(w)=f^{(n)}(w)-\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\ell_k(f)w^k,
\]
with both sums empty when $N=0$. Then $K_N:X\to Y$ is bounded and
has rank at most $N$. The Taylor series for $f^{(n)}$ and
\eqref{eq:interior-coefficient-bound} give
\[
 \max_{|w|\le\rho}|u_{N,f}(w)|
       +\max_{|w|\le\rho}|u_{N,f}'(w)|
   \le C_{X,n,R,\rho}(N+1)(\rho/R)^N\|f\|_X.
\]
Indeed, after factoring out $\|f\|_X$, the first bound is a geometric
tail. For the derivative, sum
$\rho^{-1}\sum_{k\ge N}k(\rho/R)^k$.
Since $(D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}-K_N)f=\phi(u_{N,f}\circ\varphi)$,
equation \eqref{eq:interior-target-bound} yields
\[
 \|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}-K_N\|_{X\to Y} \le C B(N+1)(\rho/R)^N \le
 C'\|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}\|_{X\to Y}\eta^N.
\]
The last step uses $\rho/R<\eta$. This proves \eqref{eq:interior-rank-one} in operator quasi-norm. Since
$\operatorname{rank}K_N\le N<N+1$, it also bounds $a_{N+1}$.
Replacing $N$ by $N-1$ and absorbing the fixed factor $\eta^{-1}$
proves (1) for every $N\ge1$.

For the limiting rate, choose any
$\eta\in(\|\varphi\|_\infty,1)$ and then
$\rho\in(\|\varphi\|_\infty,\eta)$. The estimate in (1) gives a
limit superior at most $\eta$; let $\eta$ decrease to
$\|\varphi\|_\infty$. This argument includes
$\varphi\equiv0$, when the operator has rank at most one.

When $X,Y$ are Banach spaces, the representation and summability in
(2) give $t$-nuclearity by the stated definition for each
$0<t\le1$. No approximation property of either space is required.
For the last assertion, the defining norms of $F(2,\beta_1,0)$
and $F(2,\beta_2,0)$ are Hilbert norms.
The bounds persist under the equivalent Hilbert norms on the weighted
Dirichlet spaces. For compact maps between Hilbert spaces, the
approximation numbers are the singular values; see
\cite{Simon2005}. Their geometric bound makes their $t$th powers
summable for every $t>0$, proving membership in $\mathcal S_t$.

label: lem:Dirichlet-derivative-reduction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Dirichlet-derivative-reduction}
Let $\beta\in\mathbb R$, let $m\ge0$ be an integer, and suppose
$\beta+2m>1$. Differentiation $f\mapsto f^{(m)}$ maps
$\mathcal D_\beta$ boundedly onto $A_{\beta+2m-2}^2$ and has the
bounded right inverse $J^m$, where $J$ is integration from zero and
$J^0=I$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Dirichlet-higher-derivative}
 \|f^{(m)}\|_{A_{\beta+2m-2}^2}^2
 \approx\sum_{k\ge m}(k+1)^{1-\beta}|c_k|^2,
               \qquad f(z)=\sum_{k\ge0}c_kz^k,
\end{equation}
and
\[
 \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal D_\beta}\le1}|f^{(m)}(w)|
       \approx(1-|w|^2)^{-(\beta+2m)/2}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\gamma=\beta+2m-2>-1$. Orthogonality and the displayed monomial
norm formula give, for $k\ge m$,
$\|(z^k)^{(m)}\|_{A_\gamma^2}^2\approx
(k+1)^{2m-\gamma-1}=(k+1)^{1-\beta}$.
Summation proves \eqref{eq:Dirichlet-higher-derivative}, first for
polynomials and then for power series by monotone convergence.
Integrating a Bergman function $m$ times and assigning zero to the
first $m$ coefficients proves boundedness of the right inverse.
The Bergman evaluation norm is comparable to
$(1-|w|^2)^{-(\gamma+2)/2}$, by its reproducing kernel
$(\gamma+1)(1-\overline wz)^{-\gamma-2}$; the derivative map and its
right inverse give both bounds in the last assertion.
head: environment

label: lem:Schatten-kernel-tail
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Schatten-kernel-tail}
Let $A>0$, $n\ge1$, $t>0$, and let $M$ be a positive integer with
$(M-A)t>1$. Put
\[
 H_{ik}=\frac{\delta_i^{A+n-1}\delta_k^{M-A}}
                   {|1-\overline{a_k}a_i|^{M+n-1}}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Schatten-kernel-tail}
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_i
       \sum_{d(a_i,a_k)>R}H_{ik}^{\,t}=0.
\end{equation}
For each $R>0$, the marked points can be divided into finitely many
sets within each of which distinct points have distance greater
than $R$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The spacing of the marked points gives a fixed $r_0>0$ such that the
disks $\{w:d(w,a_k)<r_0\}$ are disjoint. On each disk,
$1-|w|^2\approx\delta_k$,
$|1-\overline wa_i|\approx|1-\overline{a_k}a_i|$, and its area is
comparable to $\delta_k^2$, with constants independent of $i,k$.
Consequently, with $b=A+n-1>0$ and $R>r_0$,
\[
 \sum_{d(a_i,a_k)>R}H_{ik}^{\,t}
 \le C(1-|a_i|^2)^{bt}
       \int_{d(a_i,w)>R-r_0}
       \frac{(1-|w|^2)^{(M-A)t-2}}
            {|1-\overline wa_i|^{(M+n-1)t}}\,dA(w).
\]
Under the substitution $w=\sigma_{a_i}(\zeta)$, the right-hand side
becomes
\[
 C\int_{|\zeta|>\tanh(R-r_0)}
    \frac{(1-|\zeta|^2)^v}{|1-\overline{a_i}\zeta|^\lambda}\,dA(\zeta),
 \qquad v=(M-A)t-2,\quad \lambda=(M-2A-n+1)t.
\]
All factors involving $1-|a_i|^2$ cancel. Here $v>-1$ and
$v+2-\lambda=bt>0$. Choose
$0<\varepsilon<\min\{v+1,bt\}$. The elementary subcritical kernel
estimate gives
\[
 \sup_{a\in\mathbb D}\int_{\mathbb D}
       \frac{(1-|\zeta|^2)^{v-\varepsilon}}
            {|1-\overline a\zeta|^\lambda}\,dA(\zeta)<\infty.
\]
For completeness, this follows by angular integration: for
$\lambda>1$, the angular integral is bounded by
$C(1-r)^{1-\lambda}$; for $\lambda=1$ it is bounded by
$C\log(e/(1-r))$; and for $\lambda<1$ it is uniformly bounded.
The remaining radial integrals converge because
$v-\varepsilon>-1$ and $\lambda<v-\varepsilon+2$.
Factoring $(1-|\zeta|^2)^\varepsilon$ out on the restricted region
now bounds the preceding tail by
$C(1-\tanh^2(R-r_0))^\varepsilon$, uniformly in $i$. This proves
\eqref{eq:Schatten-kernel-tail}.

Finally, any disk of a fixed hyperbolic radius contains at most a
fixed number of marked points. Indeed, the disjoint disks of radius
$r_0$ about these points lie in a slightly larger disk, and their
areas with respect to $(1-|z|^2)^{-2}\,dA(z)$ are equal and positive.
Join two marked points when their distance is at most $R$. The
resulting graph has uniformly bounded degree. A greedy coloring of
its countable set of vertices uses finitely many colors, and each
color class has the required separation.

label: lem:two-jet-Schatten
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:two-jet-Schatten}
Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, let $n\ge0$ be an integer with
$\alpha+2n>1$, and let $t>0$. Let $\tau$ be a positive
$\sigma$-finite Borel measure on $\mathbb D$, let $u,v$ be finite-valued
measurable functions, and let $\varphi$ be an analytic self-map of
$\mathbb D$. Set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  \mathcal Lf(z)&=u(z)f^{(n)}(\varphi(z))
                  +v(z)f^{(n+1)}(\varphi(z)),\\
  d_k&=\delta_k^{-\alpha-2n}
            \int_{\varphi^{-1}(Q_k)}|u|^2\,d\tau
       +\delta_k^{-\alpha-2n-2}
            \int_{\varphi^{-1}(Q_k)}|v|^2\,d\tau.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The formula defines an operator in
$\mathcal S_t(\mathcal D_\alpha,L^2(\tau))$ if and only if
$\sum_kd_k^{t/2}<\infty$. In that case
\[
 \|\mathcal L\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t\approx\sum_kd_k^{t/2}.
\]
The constants depend only on $\alpha,n,t$ and the partition.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\gamma=\alpha+2n-2>-1$ and consider
$Bh=u(h\circ\varphi)+v(h'\circ\varphi)$ on $A_\gamma^2$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:Dirichlet-derivative-reduction} gives
$\mathcal L=B\partial^n$ and $B=\mathcal L J^n$, with the derivative
map and its right inverse bounded. The ideal inequality therefore
reduces both the criterion and the norm comparison to $B$.
The exponents in $d_k$ are now $\gamma+2$ and $\gamma+4$.

Suppose $\sum_kd_k^{t/2}<\infty$, and denote the weighted pull-back
measures of $|u|^2d\tau$ and $|v|^2d\tau$ by $\mu_0$ and $\mu_1$.
They are finite, since $d_k$ is bounded and
$\sum_k\delta_k^{\gamma+2}<\infty$.
By \eqref{eq:Bergman-trace-criterion}, the embeddings from
$A_\gamma^2$ into $L^2(\mu_0)$ and from $A_{\gamma+2}^2$ into
$L^2(\mu_1)$ belong to $\mathcal S_t$. The corresponding weighted
composition maps into $L^2(\tau)$ have the same singular values:
their squared norms on each function give the same quadratic forms
as the embeddings. Differentiation maps $A_\gamma^2$ boundedly into
$A_{\gamma+2}^2$, as follows from the monomial norm formula.
The ideal and quasi-triangle inequalities yield
\[
 \|B\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t\le C\sum_kd_k^{t/2}.
\]

Conversely, suppose $B\in\mathcal S_t$. Testing $1$ and $z$ gives
$u=B1\in L^2(\tau)$ and $v=Bz-u\varphi\in L^2(\tau)$, so each
$d_k$ is finite. Set $A=(\gamma+2)/2$ and fix an integer $M$ such
that $M>A+1$ and $(M-A)t>1$. For $e=0,1$, put
\[
 g_{k,e}(z)=\frac{\delta_k^{M+e-A}}
                    {(1-\overline{a_k}z)^{M+e}}.
\]
Since $H(2,2,(\gamma+1)/2)=A_\gamma^2$ with equivalent norms,
Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-estimates} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Schatten-atom-synthesis}
 \left\|\sum_kc_kg_{k,e}\right\|_{A_\gamma^2}
                      \le C\left(\sum_k|c_k|^2\right)^{1/2}
\end{equation}
for every finite sum. The bound is also uniform if $e=e_k$ varies
with $k$, by splitting the sum into its two possible values.

Let $\Pi_i$ be multiplication by $\mathbf1_{\varphi^{-1}(Q_i)}$
in $L^2(\tau)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:two-kernels}, with orders $0,1$,
gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Schatten-local-diagonal}
 d_i\le C\sum_{e=0}^1\|\Pi_i B g_{i,e}\|_{L^2(\tau)}^2.
\end{equation}
Use Lemma~\ref{lem:Schatten-kernel-tail} with its order equal to $1$,
so that
$H_{ik}=\delta_i^A\delta_k^{M-A}|1-\overline{a_k}a_i|^{-M}$.
For $w\in Q_i$, direct differentiation gives
\[
 \delta_i^A|g_{k,e}(w)|+
 \delta_i^{A+1}|g_{k,e}'(w)|\le C H_{ik}.
\]
Here $|1-\overline{a_k}w|\approx|1-\overline{a_k}a_i|$, and both
$\delta_i$ and $\delta_k$ are bounded by a fixed multiple of this
denominator. Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Schatten-local-offdiagonal}
 \|\Pi_i B g_{k,e}\|_{L^2(\tau)}\le C d_i^{1/2}H_{ik}.
\end{equation}

For $t\ge2$, let $V_e:\ell^2\to A_\gamma^2$ be the bounded
synthesis map in \eqref{eq:Schatten-atom-synthesis}. If
$(\mathbf e_k)$ is the coordinate basis of $\ell^2$, the basis
inequality gives
\[
 \sum_k\|BV_e\mathbf e_k\|_{L^2(\tau)}^t
       \le\|BV_e\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t
       \le C\|B\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t.
\]
Raise \eqref{eq:Schatten-local-diagonal} to the power $t/2$, sum over
$i$, and use that $\Pi_i$ is a contraction. This proves the lower
norm bound when $t\ge2$.

Now let $0<t<2$. Fix the constants in
\eqref{eq:Schatten-local-diagonal}--\eqref{eq:Schatten-local-offdiagonal}.
Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose $R$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:Schatten-kernel-tail} such that
$\sup_i\sum_{d(a_i,a_k)>R}H_{ik}^t<\varepsilon$, and partition the
marked points into finitely many $R$-separated sets.
Take a finite subset $F$ of one such set, omitting indices with
$d_i=0$. For each $i\in F$, choose $e_i\in\{0,1\}$ so that
\[
 \|\Pi_i B g_{i,e_i}\|_{L^2(\tau)}\ge c d_i^{1/2},
 \qquad h_i=\frac{\Pi_i B g_{i,e_i}}
                      {\|\Pi_i B g_{i,e_i}\|_{L^2(\tau)}}.
\]
The $h_i$ are orthonormal because their supports are disjoint.
Thus $Uh=(\langle h,h_i\rangle)_{i\in F}$ is a contraction, and
$V_Fc=\sum_{i\in F}c_i g_{i,e_i}$ has uniformly bounded norm by
\eqref{eq:Schatten-atom-synthesis}.
The matrix $Z=UBV_F$ satisfies
$\|Z\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t\le C\|B\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t$ and
\[
 Z_{ii}=\|\Pi_i B g_{i,e_i}\|_{L^2(\tau)}\ge c d_i^{1/2},
 \qquad |Z_{ik}|\le C d_i^{1/2}H_{ik}\quad(i\ne k).
\]
Let $Z_0$ be its diagonal part. By
\eqref{eq:Schatten-matrix-entries},
\[
 \|Z-Z_0\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t
 \le C\sum_{i\in F}d_i^{t/2}\sum_{\substack{k\in F\\k\ne i}}H_{ik}^t
 \le C\varepsilon\sum_{i\in F}d_i^{t/2}.
\]
The quasi-triangle inequality now yields
\[
 c^t\sum_{i\in F}d_i^{t/2}
 \le\|Z_0\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t
 \le C_t\|B\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t+
                         C_t'\varepsilon\sum_{i\in F}d_i^{t/2}.
\]
Choose $\varepsilon$ so that $C_t'\varepsilon<c^t/2$ and absorb
the last term. The bound is independent of the finite set $F$.
Exhaust each separated set and add over the finitely many sets to get
$\sum_i d_i^{t/2}\le C\|B\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t$.
Together with the initial derivative reduction, this proves the
criterion and both norm estimates, including $n=0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Write
\[
 Bf=\phi'(f^{(n)}\circ\varphi)
          +\phi\varphi'(f^{(n+1)}\circ\varphi),
 \qquad \ell(f)=\phi(0)f^{(n)}(\varphi(0)).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:two-jet-Schatten}, with
$\alpha=\beta_1$, $u=\phi'$, $v=\phi\varphi'$ and
$d\tau=(1-|z|^2)^{\beta_2}\,dA$, characterizes $B$ as a map from
$\mathcal D_{\beta_1}$ to $L^2(\tau)$. Whenever it is bounded its
range consists of analytic functions, so it takes values in
$A_{\beta_2}^2$ and has the same singular values with this codomain.
The evaluation estimate in
Lemma~\ref{lem:Dirichlet-derivative-reduction} gives
\[
 \|\ell\|_{\mathcal D_{\beta_1}^*}
       \approx\frac{|\phi(0)|}{(1-|\varphi(0)|^2)^{(\beta_1+2n)/2}}.
\]
In particular, this functional is always bounded for fixed analytic
symbols.

The maps $h\mapsto h'$ from $\mathcal D_{\beta_2}$ to
$A_{\beta_2}^2$ and $Jg(z)=\int_0^zg(\zeta)\,d\zeta$ in the
opposite direction are bounded. Evaluation at zero is bounded as
well, and $\|1\|_{\mathcal D_{\beta_2}}=1$. The identity
\[
 D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}f=\ell(f)\,1+JBf
\]
therefore proves, by the ideal and quasi-triangle inequalities,
\[
 \|D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t
       \approx\|\ell\|_{\mathcal D_{\beta_1}^*}^{\,t}
                     +\|B\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t
\]
whenever the terms on either side are finite. For the reverse
inequalities, compose $D_{\phi,\varphi}^{n}$ with evaluation at zero
and with differentiation. This proves \textup{(1)}$\Longleftrightarrow$\textup{(2)}, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:two-jet-Schatten} gives
\eqref{eq:Dirichlet-Schatten-norm}.

To compare (2) and (3), a disk $\Delta(w,\eta)$ with $w\in Q_i$
meets only a bounded number of rectangles $Q_k$ with comparable
boundary distances. Thus its two normalized masses are bounded by
$C\sum_{k\in N(i)}v_k$, for a uniformly bounded neighbor collection.
The invariant area of $Q_i$ is comparable to one, so integration and
the inequality for a positive power of a finite sum bound (3) by
$C\sum_kv_k^{t/2}$. Conversely, subdivide each $Q_k$ into a fixed
finite number of sets with pseudohyperbolic diameter less than
$\eta/4$. For each such set there is a disk of centers, of fixed
positive invariant area, whose $\eta$-disks contain that set.
Its two normalized masses therefore bound from below the corresponding
partial contributions to $v_k$. Summing those finitely many
contributions and using bounded overlap of the center disks gives
$\sum_kv_k^{t/2}$ bounded by (3). Both arguments work for every
$t>0$, using constants for a finite sum rather than a triangle
inequality that would fail at a small exponent.

For $t=2$, the sequence sum is $\sum_{j,l}v_{j,l}$. On
$Q_{j,l}$ one has $1-|w|^2\approx\delta_j$. Summing over the
partition turns this sum into the two integrals in the statement,
up to fixed constants. The definition of the pull-back measures
then gives the direct symbol integral in the statement. This proves
the Hilbert--Schmidt assertion as well.

label: thm:monomial-exact
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:monomial-exact}
Let $\beta_1,\beta_2\in\mathbb R$, let $m,n\ge0$ be integers, and
let $\rho\in\mathbb C$ with $|\rho|\le1$. Take
$\phi(z)=z^m$ and $\varphi(z)=\rho z$.

\textup{(a)} Suppose $0<|\rho|\le1$. For $k\ge n$, put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:monomial-weights}
 \sigma_k=\frac{k!}{(k-n)!}|\rho|^{k-n}
        (k+1)^{(\beta_1-1)/2}
        (k-n+m+1)^{(1-\beta_2)/2}.
\end{equation}
Then $D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}:\mathcal D_{\beta_1}\to
\mathcal D_{\beta_2}$ is bounded if and only if
$\sup_{k\ge n}\sigma_k<\infty$. Under this condition,
\[
 \|D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}\|=\sup_{k\ge n}\sigma_k,
 \qquad
 \|D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}\|_e=\limsup_{k\to\infty}\sigma_k.
\]
It is compact if and only if $\sigma_k\to0$. In the compact case,
its nonzero singular values are the nonincreasing rearrangement of
$(\sigma_k)_{k\ge n}$. For every $t>0$,
\[
 D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}\in\mathcal S_t
       \iff\sum_{k=n}^{\infty}\sigma_k^t<\infty,
 \qquad
 \|D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}\|_{\mathcal S_t}^t
       =\sum_{k=n}^{\infty}\sigma_k^t
\]
when the sum is finite.

\textup{(b)} If $0<|\rho|<1$, the operator belongs to every
$\mathcal S_t$, $t>0$, and
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}a_N(D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n})^{1/N}=|\rho|.
\]
If $|\rho|=1$, the exact parameter conditions are
\begin{enumerate}
 \renewcommand{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}{\textup{(\arabic{enumi})}}
 \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
 \item boundedness $\iff\beta_2-\beta_1\ge2n$;
 \item compactness $\iff\beta_2-\beta_1>2n$;
 \item membership in $\mathcal S_t$
          $\iff\beta_2-\beta_1>2n+2/t$.
\end{enumerate}
At $\beta_2-\beta_1=2n$, the essential norm is exactly $1$.

\textup{(c)} If $\rho=0$, the operator has rank one, with its only
nonzero singular value equal to
\[
 n!(n+1)^{(\beta_1-1)/2}(m+1)^{(1-\beta_2)/2}.
\]
In particular it belongs to every Schatten class. All assertions
include $n=0$, with $0!=1$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The functions $e_k^{(\beta)}(z)=(k+1)^{(\beta-1)/2}z^k$ form an
orthonormal basis of $\mathcal D_\beta$. For $k<n$ the image of
$e_k^{(\beta_1)}$ is zero, whereas for $k\ge n$ and $\rho\ne0$,
\[
 D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}e_k^{(\beta_1)}
   =\frac{k!}{(k-n)!}\rho^{k-n}(k+1)^{(\beta_1-1)/2}
       (k-n+m+1)^{(1-\beta_2)/2}e_{k-n+m}^{(\beta_2)}.
\]
The target basis indices are distinct. Orthogonality therefore gives,
for every finite sum $f=\sum_kc_ke_k^{(\beta_1)}$,
\[
 \|D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}f\|_{\mathcal D_{\beta_2}}^2
             =\sum_{k\ge n}|c_k|^2\sigma_k^2.
\]
This proves the boundedness criterion and the exact norm. When the
sequence is bounded, density of polynomials yields the bounded
extension, which agrees with the analytic formula by local uniform
convergence.

Keeping the first finitely many nonzero columns gives a finite-rank
approximation, and the norm of the discarded part is the supremum
of the remaining $\sigma_k$. Hence the essential norm is at most
$\limsup_k\sigma_k$. Conversely, for any compact operator $K$,
$\|Ke_k^{(\beta_1)}\|\to0$, since an orthonormal sequence is weakly
null. Thus
\[
 \|D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}-K\|
   \ge\limsup_{k\to\infty}
         \|(D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}-K)e_k^{(\beta_1)}\|
   \ge\limsup_{k\to\infty}\sigma_k.
\]
Taking the infimum over $K$ proves the asserted essential norm and
compactness criterion. In the compact case, the positive operator
$(D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n})^*D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n}$ is diagonal in the
source basis, with diagonal entries $0$ for $k<n$ and $\sigma_k^2$
for $k\ge n$. Its eigenvalues give the singular-value and Schatten
formulas in (a).

Put $\gamma=n+(\beta_1-\beta_2)/2$. Directly from
\eqref{eq:monomial-weights},
\[
 \frac{\sigma_k}{|\rho|^{k-n}k^\gamma}\longrightarrow1
                                    \qquad(k\to\infty).
\]
For $|\rho|=1$, this gives all three conditions in (b), since
$\sum_k k^{t\gamma}<\infty$ if and only if $t\gamma<-1$. If $\gamma=0$, then $\sigma_k\to1$,
which proves the exact essential norm at the boundary.

If $0<|\rho|<1$, exponential decay makes
$\sum_k\sigma_k^t$ finite for every $t>0$. Moreover,
$\sigma_{k+1}/\sigma_k\to|\rho|<1$, so the sequence is eventually
strictly decreasing. It is positive and tends to zero; consequently,
a sufficiently late tail lies below every earlier term. Its
nonincreasing rearrangement therefore satisfies
$a_N(D_{z^m,\rho z}^{n})=\sigma_{n+N-1}$ for all sufficiently large
$N$. Taking $N$th roots proves the limit in (b).

Finally, if $\rho=0$, the formula is simply
$D_{z^m,0}^{n}f=f^{(n)}(0)z^m$. The functional $f\mapsto f^{(n)}(0)$
has norm $n!(n+1)^{(\beta_1-1)/2}$ on the source, and $z^m$ has
norm $(m+1)^{(1-\beta_2)/2}$ in the target. Their product is the
only nonzero singular value of this rank-one operator. This proves
(c) without assigning a value to $0^0$.
